original_value: Healthcare has been the industry with the highest boom in terms of both revenue and data. With so much of electronic health records, the security has been the need of the hour. To make this critical information more secure, there has been an urge to use the blockchain technology. Therefore, researches came up with a solution of blockchain technology in medical healthcare that will not only protect data from being tampered but will also ensure that the data leakage is stopped. This technology could preserve data and thus guarantee reliability. And if this technology is used along with cloud computing technology, problems related to storage can also be vanished, because cloud is trusted for storing and managing data. Also, the blockchain can address the security issues of the cloud. Indeed, medical data sharing and storing with Blockchain‐based cloud can address a lot of issues of medical data. The main aim of this paper is to present the current state‐of‐the‐art on blockchain‐based medical healthcare system. We have clearly discussed several existing works on the same domain and also presented a comparative study among the published works.

result.paraphrase: Healthcare has emerged as the fastest-growing industry in both revenue and data volume. With the widespread use of electronic health records, security has become an urgent necessity. To better safeguard this critical information, blockchain technology has been increasingly proposed. Researchers have therefore developed a blockchain-based solution for medical healthcare that not only helps prevent data tampering but also stops data leakage. By preserving data integrity, this technology can improve reliability. When combined with cloud computing, it can also eliminate storage-related issues, since the cloud is trusted for data storage and management. Blockchain can further help resolve cloud security concerns. In fact, storing and sharing medical data through a blockchain-based cloud can address many challenges in medical data management. The main purpose of this paper is to present the current state of the art in blockchain-based medical healthcare systems. We discuss several existing works in this domain and provide a comparative study of the published literature.
